page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tier of modern cloud hardware. In CPU-focused tests, the ecs.c5.xlarge scored 1103.19 in stress-ng single-core and 2934.5 in multi-core performance, both falling into the bottom 25% bracket. Geekbench results mirror this trend, with a single-core score of 987.0 and a multi-core score of 2173.0. Memory performance is also constrained, with uncached read bandwidth measured at 20.58 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 18.68 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute resources without the risk of noisy-neighbor CPU throttling common in burstable instances. However, the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a performance-per-resource tradeoff compared to newer generations. This instance is best suited for lightweight compute-focused workloads, basic web serving, small-scale Redis deployments, and entry-level compilation or text processing tasks that do not require high memory density or local storage performance.
